subject: Post-demo technical touchpoint: SDK, auth, routing, embeddings, and prompt hygiene
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@novushealth.ai>, Novus Health Eng Team <eng@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo technical touchpoint: SDK, auth, routing, embeddings, and prompt hygiene

Hi Sophie + Novus eng team —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick technical recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the pilot work: we picked up a few clear priorities during the call.

1) SDK & quickstart
- Goal: get a minimal SDK integration into your staging service within 2 dev days. We’ll provide a short snippet (attached) and a sample Node + Python client.
- Action: Dev, can you confirm language preference (node/python) and whether you want the cookiecutter repo or a tarball?

2) Auth model
- Options we discussed: API key (fast), short-lived mTLS tokens (recommended for Prod), or OIDC integration to your IdP (best for SSO + rotation).
- Recommendation for pilot: start with scoped API keys + IP-restricted gateway, then move to OIDC in parallel with your security team.

3) Routing & model variants
- We can route by region and by latency/cost tiers. For Novus, suggest: region=us-east (primary), fallback=us-west, failover to smaller quantized model for non-critical traffic.
- We’ll surface routing rules in the SDK config (env overrides).

4) Structured output / tool calling
- If you want deterministic JSON responses we’ll use the structured output mode (schema-first) + function/tool calling for actions (patient lookup, eligibility check).
- We’ll include a schema template and an example tool-calling flow for your eligibility microservice.

5) Embeddings & re-ranker plan
- For clinical note retrieval: we recommend sentence-transformer embeddings with a two-stage retrieval (ANN -> re-ranker) to reduce hallucination.
- We’ll provide a baseline embedding batch job and an example re-ranker prompt template.

6) Prompt templates & governance (versioning + injection mitigations)
- Centralize templates in a single repo (prompt-template-v1.json attached). Version each template and keep a changelog.
- Mitigations: input sanitation (strip HTML/control chars), explicit system prompt markers, user instruction whitelists, and response validators on structured fields.
- Red team: run a small adversarial suite against your most sensitive flows (PII, clinical guidance) before Prod cutover.

Attachments: novus-mvp-checklist.xlsx (MVP scope + owners), prompt-template-v1.json, sdk-auth-snippet.md

Proposed next steps:
- Dev: confirm preferred SDK language and staging URL by EOD Wed (2027-05-05).
- Sophie: confirm whether security wants API key pilot or immediate OIDC (we can support both).
- We’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for SDK + auth on Fri; I’ll send a calendar invite once Dev confirms language.

If anything above is off from what you heard, please call it out. Otherwise we’ll move forward on the API-key scoped pilot and the embedding baseline job.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Subject: Re: Post-demo technical touchpoint: SDK, auth, routing, embeddings, and prompt hygiene

Alex —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick notes from our side after syncing with the engineering leads:

- Priority: Auth + embeddings (we need a secure pilot to validate clinical retrieval).
- For the pilot we are comfortable starting with scoped API keys (Dev will lock those down in staging). Long-term we want OIDC, but security wants to see the pilot telemetry first.
- SDK language: Node (we run the API gateway in Node). Please send the cookiecutter project.
- Re-ranker: yes to the two-stage approach; can you annotate the prompt-template with a few negative examples and a scorer threshold?

Can you also call out any data retention/PII flags we should be aware of for the embeddings job? Our security team will want that up front.

If you can get the Node quickstart + API key setup instructions by EOD Thu (2027-05-06) we’ll slot resource time to onboard.

Thanks,
Sophie Lane
Director of Product, Novus Health
sophie.lane@novushealth.ai

Subject: Internal: Red-team scope + prompt governance checklist for Novus (internal follow-up)

Alex / Rishi / Dev —

Internal note for our owners before we move forward with Novus: we should keep the red-team scope tight for the pilot and capture results in a small report for their security team. Proposed internal items: 

- Red-team tests (priority): prompt injection attempts on retrieval + re-ranker, malformed function-calls, schema poisoning (structured output).
- Prompt governance: maintain a versioned prompt repo (prompt-template-v1.json) with template-level test vectors and a changelog. All changes >minor require a quick review and a rolling tag (v1.0, v1.1, etc.).
- Validation layer: add JSON schema validation on the service side for any structured outputs and a scoring threshold for re-ranker outputs.
- Telemetry: log model variant, prompt version, and request hashes (no raw PII) for debugging/regression.

Rishi: can you produce the embedding retention + hashing guidance by 2027-05-09 as Alex outlined. Dev: please confirm whether you want the cookiecutter or tarball; I recommend cookiecutter so we can enforce the standard config files.

I’ll prepare a 1-page red-team checklist and a short instruction doc for the prompt repo (templates + PR process). Once we have the Node quickstart in staging, we’ll run the red-team suite in staging only.

Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Retrieval & Safety | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
